validity_findings.finding: valid_token never experienced triple_br (0/180 reps across all 9 content-type x size conditions; each condition valid_token encoding_scenarios_seen unique_count=5 missing triple_br, while no_auth/invalid_token/expired_token each have 6/6 including triple_br). Root cause: run_experiment.py creates scenario_rng=Random(SEED+7919) per condition then immediately consumes one draw for the CDN proxy connectivity test (requests.get through proxy) before the 80 shuffled measured requests. The 81-draw sequence shifted by 1 maps triple_br draws away from valid_token positions under uniform random choice. The frozen question explicitly asks whether iterative decompression restores discrimination under double AND triple brotli; triple survival for the distinct success body (the only body that separates valid_token from error collapse) is therefore UNTESTED. Decompressed_hash_variation all_same=true for valid_token is true but vacuous for triple layer. Decision rule clause 4 literally passes on observed data, but does not establish the claimed triple coverage.

validity_findings.finding: Iterative decompress_body (brotli->gzip->identity looping to max_depth=5) correctly restores known bodies when tested in isolation: manual recompression of a 1KB valid JSON body (brotli quality 6) through double (74B) and triple (82B) wrapping decompresses to original identical bytes, and all observed error-state triple_br bodies (82B) decompress to true bodies (e.g., no_auth JSON 6fb10d...). For valid_token, double_br IS observed (5-7 reps per condition) and decompresses correctly to d15e53... matching single-layer hashes, proving double fix for success body. Triple fix for success body inferred via error-body evidence and manual test, not via measured valid_token triple observations. No over-decompression of plain text: plain text b'hello' returns unchanged, and gc/garbled paths succeed via brotli.

validity_findings.finding: Uniform random scenario selection with N=20 per state per condition yields high variance in per-state counts and zero-coverage risk for a specific scenario. With 6 scenarios uniform, expected per-state count ~3.3, P(zero of a given scenario in 20 draws) ~ 0.026, P(zero across 9 conditions for same state) ~ 0.79 if independent. The observed systematic zero (same shift) is deterministically worse than random: same shuffled plan reused per condition and same RNG sequence means missing scenario repeats across conditions. Stratified or round-robin assignment would guarantee coverage at N=20.
